speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any changes in your coordination, such as shuffling gait or stumbling, and do you experience any numbness or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

Given the combination of progressive lower motor neuron signs (gait difficulty, urinary incontinence) and upper motor neuron signs (speech slurring) over several months, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of ALS. I have made this diagnosis based on the established clinical evidence; no further diagnostic tests are required at this time.
